    StartersSafari camp beef samosas with mint yoghurtCrisp fried triangles of curried beef, carrot and peas, mint yoghurtHow to make it400g beef mince1 onion, diced2 garlic cloves, crushed2 tsp curry powder1 tsp garam masala1 carrot, grated100g frozen peas1 small bunch coriander, chopped6 spring rolls of wrappers1 L vegetable oil, for frying200g Greek yoghurt1 small bunch mint, choppedFry the mince, onion and garlic until browned. Add the curry powder, garam masala, carrot and peas and cook, then stir through the coriander and cool.Cut the wrappers into strips, spoon filling at one end and fold into triangles, sealing with water.Fry in the vegetable oil at 180°C until golden, working in batches.Mix the yoghurt with the mint and a pinch of salt for dipping.Serve the samosas hot with the mint yoghurt.Monastery momos with chilli tomato sauceSteamed pork and ginger dumplings with fresh chilli tomato sauceHow to make it400g pork mince1 tbsp grated ginger3 garlic cloves, 2 crushed for the filling and 1 for the sauce3 spring onions, sliced1 tbsp soy sauce1 tsp sesame oil24 round dumpling wrappers2 tomatoes2 red chillies1 tbsp white vinegar1 pinch saltMix the pork with the ginger, two of the garlic cloves, spring onions, soy and sesame oil.Place a teaspoon of filling in each wrapper, wet the edges and pleat closed.Steam in a lined steamer over boiling water.Blitz the tomatoes, chillies, remaining garlic, salt and vinegar, then simmer to make the sauce.Fried plantain with peri periBest eaten after leaving a rhino. Ask Ace.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsSafari grilled chicken with chapatiLemon chilli grilled chicken, chapati and tomato kachumbari saladHow to make it1kg chicken thigh fillets2 lemons, juiced3 garlic cloves, crushed1 tsp chilli flakes1 tsp paprika4 tbsp vegetable oil300g plain flour1 tsp salt3 tomatoes, diced1 red onion, diced1 small bunch coriander1 lime, juicedMarinate the chicken with the lemon juice, garlic, chilli flakes, paprika, some of the oil and salt.Marinate in the fridge.Mix the flour, salt, remaining oil and warm water into a dough, knead, then rest.Roll the dough into rounds and dry-fry each side in a hot pan.Grill the chicken, turning once, until cooked through.Toss the tomatoes, onion, coriander and lime juice for the kachumbari and serve with the chicken and chapati.Wachootoo sweet potato and peanut stewBrought to the peace feast between the Wachati and the WachootooHow to make it800g sweet potato, in chunks1 onion, diced2 garlic cloves, crushed20g ginger, grated1 tsp ground cumin1 red chilli, chopped400g tinned chopped tomatoes120g crunchy peanut butter500ml vegetable stock100g baby spinach300g long grain rice1 lime40g roasted peanuts1 tbsp vegetable oilSoften the onion, garlic, ginger, chilli and cumin in the oil.Add the sweet potato, tomatoes, peanut butter and stock and simmer until tender. Meanwhile cook the rice.Stir through the spinach until wilted.Serve over rice with lime and chopped peanuts.SweetsCoconut and cardamom mandaziFried coconut cardamom doughnutsHow to make it300g self-raising flour120g caster sugar1 tsp ground cardamom200ml coconut milk1 egg1 L vegetable oil, for frying4 tbsp honeyMix the flour, half the sugar, cardamom and a pinch of salt. Stir in the coconut milk and egg to a soft dough, then knead briefly.Rest the dough.Roll out 1cm thick and cut into triangles.Fry in oil at 170°C, turning, until puffed and golden.
